requirement: Describe the study as a prospective, single-center, single-arm, open-label mixed-methods feasibility pilot in Veterans with prediabetes; do not invent a concurrent control group or randomized treatment comparison.

evidence.text: The objectives explicitly identify a single-arm mixed-methods pilot testing feasibility, acceptability and weight loss among Veterans with prediabetes.

requirement: Represent VA LC-DPP as a one-year group-based behavioral program with 16 weekly one-hour sessions followed by eight one-hour sessions once or twice monthly, together with low-carbohydrate eating, self-weighing, food logging and physical-activity logging.

evidence.text: The consent describes 16 weekly sessions plus eight later sessions, one hour each, with diet, self-weighing and food/activity logs over one year.

requirement: Use baseline, 6-month and 12-month quantitative assessments, with body weight also measured at every group session and the 6- and 12-month laboratory assessments corresponding to sessions 16 and 24.

evidence.text: The synopsis schedules surveys and waist measures at baseline, 6 and 12 months and weight at every session; the laboratory section maps 6 and 12 months to sessions 16 and 24.

requirement: Before finalization, operationalize recruitment and retention feasibility with explicit numerators, denominators, time windows and handling of screened, eligible, consented, enrolled, withdrawn and assessment-completing participants.

evidence.text: Enrollment and retention are named primary feasibility outcomes without operational numerators, denominators or thresholds.

requirement: Before finalization, define acceptability and adherence summaries with denominators and time windows for session attendance, self-weighing, food tracking and physical-activity-goal or log completion, keeping these measures distinct from weight loss.

evidence.text: Acceptability includes session attendance and qualitative feedback; participants are asked to self-weigh and maintain food and physical-activity logs.

requirement: Analyze body weight as change from baseline at 6 and 12 months and separately summarize achievement of at least 5% baseline body-weight loss at each time point, without describing comparison with historical programs as a randomized causal effect.

evidence.text: The protocol names weight change and achievement of at least 5% loss and says published MOVE!/DPP data, rather than a concurrent arm, may be compared descriptively.

requirement: Report baseline-to-6-month and baseline-to-12-month changes separately for HbA1c, lipid measures and waist circumference, including units and the direction of improvement for each measure.

evidence.text: Blood for HbA1c and lipids and waist circumference are collected at baseline, 6 months and 12 months.

requirement: Score cravings and stress-eating measures according to their attached item-level rules and score social support as the specified item average; do not pool them into one unspecified eating-behavior composite.

evidence.text: The attachments provide the cravings and stress-eating item rules and define social support as an average.

requirement: Derive PROMIS Global Physical Health and Global Mental Health scores using the attached recoding and T-score lookup rules, preserving the stated treatment of the global-health and pain items.

evidence.text: The PROMIS attachment defines item recoding, raw sums and physical- and mental-health T-score tables.

requirement: Derive the Treatment Self-Regulation Questionnaire motivation subscales as the specified item averages for autonomous motivation, controlled motivation and amotivation, retaining their separate interpretation.

evidence.text: The attached questionnaire and scoring key map items to the three motivation subscale averages.

requirement: Convert physical-activity questionnaire responses to the specified MET-minute summaries, with explicit frequency, duration, intensity and truncation or missing-response rules.

evidence.text: The physical-activity attachment specifies MET-based scoring for reported activity.

requirement: Apply the attached fatigue and sleep item coding and raw-to-T-score conversion rules, reporting fatigue and sleep as separate outcomes.

evidence.text: The fatigue and sleep attachments provide item coding and raw-score/T-score rules.

requirement: Before finalization, define the analysis population and inclusion rule for each feasibility, quantitative and qualitative analysis; participants need not follow the low-carbohydrate diet to remain in follow-up, and data collected before withdrawal remain analyzable while no new data are collected afterward.

evidence.text: The protocol retains data collected before withdrawal, stops later collection and says following the diet is not required to remain in the study.

requirement: Use the prospective feasibility target of up to 30 participants and state that the pilot is not powered for definitive efficacy; do not substitute the later registry actual enrollment of 18 as the planned sample size.

evidence.text: The prospective protocol says recruit up to 30 and gives 30 as the maximum signed-consent enrollment, without an efficacy power calculation.

notes: The frozen registry reports actual enrollment of 18, which is execution-era metadata and not a prospective sample-size target.

requirement: For each continuous outcome, tabulate baseline and follow-up summaries and the baseline-to-6-month and baseline-to-12-month mean change with standard deviation, while also reporting effect estimates and confidence intervals suitable for an estimation-focused pilot.

evidence.text: The reference plan specifies mean change and standard deviation from baseline to 6 and 12 months for continuous outcomes.

requirement: Before using the reference paired t tests for baseline-to-6-month and baseline-to-12-month continuous changes, prespecify paired-difference diagnostics and a small-sample robust or nonparametric fallback; do not apply an unqualified t test to every continuous or ordinal score.

evidence.text: The reference plan applies paired t tests to all continuous outcomes without assumptions or a fallback.

requirement: Before finalization, replace or justify the reference's generic chi-square/Fisher approach for categorical change with a method appropriate to paired repeated observations, and define the analyzed category, denominator and treatment of missing follow-up for each binary or categorical endpoint.
acceptable_values: McNemar or exact paired alternative when applicable

evidence.text: The reference says chi-square or Fisher exact tests will assess categorical change from baseline to 6 and 12 months, without addressing pairing.

requirement: Before finalization, specify item-level scoring thresholds, handling of skipped survey questions and missed 6- or 12-month assessments, the primary missing-data assumption, and sensitivity summaries suitable for potentially informative dropout in a small single-arm study.

evidence.text: Participants may skip survey questions and have repeated 6- and 12-month assessments, but no missing-data rules are given.

requirement: Before finalization, define the 6- and 12-month qualitative interview samples and denominators, preserving purposive sampling by achievement versus nonachievement of at least 5% weight loss and treating interviews as optional.

evidence.text: The protocol plans optional semi-structured interviews at 6 and 12 months, purposively sampled by achievement versus nonachievement of at least 5% weight loss.

requirement: Analyze verbatim interview transcripts or detailed notes by directed content analysis: two investigators independently code, resolve coding in consensus conferences, begin with interview-guide topics and retain emergent patterns and themes.

evidence.text: The reference plan specifies independent coding by two investigators, joint consensus coding and directed content analysis using guide topics and emerging themes.
Interviews may be recorded and transcribed verbatim, with detailed notes if recording is declined.
